about: Open-weight image models that run on the drafting Mac, for scripts/localgen.py.
Entries are edited here rather than in Python because local tooling changes faster
than the hosted roster does: command names, model repository ids, and quantisation
all move. `python3 scripts/localgen.py doctor` checks this file against what is
actually installed and reports the difference.
The `command` field is executed directly, with no shell. Placeholders {prompt},
{width}, {height}, {steps}, {seed}, and {output} are substituted before the call.
Treat this file as code: anything written here runs on the machine.
`commercial: false` marks weights whose licence forbids shipping their output.
Those models are skipped unless --allow-non-commercial is passed, and any run that
includes them is stamped evaluation-only in the manifest and on the published sheet.
`seconds_per_image` seeds the wall-clock estimate. Once a run exists, measured
medians from its manifest are used instead.

models.label: FLUX.2 [klein] 4B
models.strengths: the best image quality that is both Apache 2.0 and small enough to run on a 16 GB machine; inherits FLUX contour and heavy blacks
models.risks: tight at 16 GB even at 4-bit, so it competes with the rest of the desktop for memory; distilled to few steps, which limits how far a prompt correction can push it

models.label: Z-Image Turbo
models.strengths: distilled to nine steps, so it is far the fastest candidate; the right tool for framing sweeps, which it does at no cost
models.risks: tuned for photographic realism and text legibility, neither of which this book wants; not a finish-quality candidate for hand-inked work

models.label: Qwen-Image (local)
models.strengths: the largest Apache 2.0 model that fits 48 GB at 8-bit; strong composition
models.risks: its advantage is text rendering, which this book actively suppresses, so most of what it is good at is wasted here

models.label: SDXL 1.0 (local)
models.strengths: renders at 1216x832, close enough to the panel slot to need no reframing, and Draw Things trains a style LoRA on-device at 16 GB; a trained SDXL beats an untrained better model for a book whose constraint is consistency
models.risks: the oldest model on the roster and the least impressive without a trained style; needs a local server running rather than a command on PATH

models.label: Chroma1-HD
models.strengths: FLUX.1-schnell rebuilt as a neutral finetuning base and relicensed Apache 2.0; the strongest commercially usable base to train this book's style on
models.risks: no first-party MLX command, so it needs ComfyUI or Draw Things standing up an HTTP endpoint first

models.label: FLUX.1 [dev] (local)
models.strengths: the reference point everyone benchmarks against, and the model with the largest style-LoRA ecosystem
models.risks: non-commercial licence: nothing it generates can appear in the book. Carry it to calibrate the rubric, then buy the winner through an API

models.label: FLUX.2 [klein] 9B
models.strengths: what a 48 GB machine could run if licensing were not a constraint; the honest upper bound on local quality
models.risks: non-commercial licence, same as FLUX.1 [dev]. Evaluation only
